title: Prove rational cost floors for matched k-port spans
body:
PR2532 leaves even-denominator k-port decoders open. This closes the class whose source and target **spans of complete port spaces agree term by term**, with arbitrary rational factors, signs, denominators and finite term counts. Supports may differ. It adds only `research/support-balanced-port-floor/`.

A nonsingular principal decoder block forces a port-to-term matching. Every matched term contains the port’s nondegenerate space on both sides and pays its full dimension. On the exact retained covers:

| Cover | Cost floor | Favorable unpaid budget | Deficit upper bound |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| PR2297, 22 five-frames plus a pair | 554, sharp in this class | 4432/9 | -554/9 |
| PR2041, 37 three-frames plus a line | 297, not claimed sharp | 2672/9 | -1/9 |

Both fail before additional physical charges under the retained nine-stage coverage law. The PR2041 result uses its literal mixed cover, not an unconstructed uniform-three completion. A further necessary bound says any positive-saving PR2297 decoder needs at least **16 terms with unmatched complete port spans and positive rank-relief credit**; this supplies no construction at 16.

`PROOF.md` gives the quantified argument and its limits. The verifier imports no predecessor executable, authenticates exact source bytes and the selected archive member, checks every group-pair tariff with two binary-rank implementations, records the principal-set witnesses, and checks rational fixtures and meaningful failure controls. General unmatched-span decoders, native realization, hosting, precision, physical/compiler admission and the outer theorem remain open. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

Validation on CPython 3.12.14 / Darwin arm64:

```sh
python3.12 -Werror -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/support-balanced-port-floor
python3.12 -I -B scripts/verify_selected_result.py
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/support-balanced-port-floor
```

Normal/optimized replay, four CLI integrity tests, seven semantic controls, all 512 binary 3x3 determinant/matching checks and publication-byte checks pass. No selected cold replay, formal compilation, hosted CI pass or independent human review is claimed.

Started from canonical main `4b82082f901945f8d0314f143576c7ad31e021fc`, then rebased onto `c7df0bb890cae0cc393cdd32dad19c3facc80992` with unchanged guidance, catalogue, selected record and scientific inputs. TASK/SOURCES pin the assignment, heads and scope change. Final overlap: 491 open PR bodies and 1,522 Discussion/comment records, plus local notes/ledger and targeted all-state queries. [Canonical claim and investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1587#discussioncomment-18965662).

Credit Sagar Thakrar/PR2532, Cinna Davis/PR2297 and PR2041, Adam Gall/PR1889 and adjacent P112 matched-frame work, Philippe Van Velzen, Tekalign/PR2782, ctoth and the retained geometry/supplier lineage. New work by Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents or independent human review. Apache-2.0.
